cases.purpose: A spec with four planted defects of different kinds. The reviewer must find each one, with the right category, and record the missing path and the tier it re-derived.

security.reason: The shared guard already covers it.

answerKey: grounding: Reused files and the plan cite src/api/auth.ts and a requireOwner guard; neither exists at baseSha.
untestable: AC-2 has a fixture and action too vague to reproduce and an Expected line (access control works correctly) that nothing can observe.
lost-requirement: the Task asks for PATCH /api/tasks/:id and that a patch can change only the title and due date; no criterion or plan step covers either.
tier: the header says S with no flags, but the change adds API routes (at least M) that read per-user data by id (security flag needed).

expect.check: verdicts/spec-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
role == "spec-reviewer" && stage == "spec" && round == 1 && taskId == "eval-tasklist-task-by-id"
covers.specSha256 equals the SHA-256 of the spec.md fixture
verdict == "changes"
checks.grounding.missingPaths contains "src/api/auth.ts" and a blocking finding has category "grounding"
a blocking finding has category "untestable" and acIds containing "AC-2"
a blocking finding has category "lost-requirement"
checks.tier.specTier == "S" && checks.tier.assessedTier != "S" && a blocking finding has category "tier"
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run, and spec.md is unchanged
Does the lost-requirement finding name the missing update (PATCH) route or the missing limit on which fields a patch may change?
Does the tier finding, or another blocking finding, say that the security flag must be set?
Does every blocking finding's requiredChange say what must become true without rewriting the criterion in full?

cases.purpose: Precision. A grounded, testable tier S bug spec must be approved, with no blocking finding invented to look thorough.

expect.check: verdicts/spec-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
verdict == "approve" && no finding has blocking == true
checks.grounding.pathsChecked >= 2 && checks.grounding.missingPaths is empty
checks.tier.specTier == "S" && checks.tier.assessedTier == "S"
findings has at most 3 entries
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run
Is every finding, if any, about something that would materially help the builder or verifier rather than a wording or design preference?

cases.purpose: Round 2. The revision fixes the one finding of round 1 but deletes AC-4 and makes AC-3 contradict an unchanged design choice. A reviewer that only rechecks its own list approves; it must read the whole diff.

tier.reason: The change adds API routes in one module, with no schema change and no new dependency.

security.reason: New routes read and write per-user data by id and parse a request body.

changes.note: AC-3 now states the status code, the empty body, and the unchanged task.

answerKey: Round 1 finding 1 (AC-3 not observable) is resolved: the Expected line is now assertable.
contradiction: AC-3 now expects status 403, while Design choices, unchanged, says to answer 404 and not 403.

lost-requirement: AC-4 (unknown fields are rejected) was deleted, although the Task requires that a patch change only the title and due date; plan steps 2 and 3 still say they serve AC-4, and AC-4 is not listed in retiredCriteria.

expect.check: verdicts/spec-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
round == 2 && checks.revisionDiffReviewed == true
resolutions has exactly one entry, with round == 1, n == 1, and status == "resolved"
verdict == "changes"
a blocking finding has category "lost-requirement"
a blocking finding has category "contradiction" and acIds containing "AC-3"
Does the lost-requirement finding identify that the criterion rejecting unknown patch fields was removed?
Does the contradiction finding set the 403 in AC-3 against the 404 in Design choices?
